title: Modernize OIDC/SAML client deps, rotate TLS libraries, and complete license/supply-chain audit
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Recent CVEs in several downstream libraries used by our SSO and token handling stacks (OIDC client, SAML toolkit, and some older OpenSSL transitive deps) require coordinated upgrades and behavioural checks. This ticket covers: 1) upgrading OIDC and SAML client libraries used in the private control plane and console auth flow; 2) moving to the latest vetted OpenSSL patch across services that link directly to native TLS stacks; 3) rotating any altered cipher suite defaults and ensuring compatibility with customer-managed HSM/KMS; 4) running a license/supply-chain audit on transitive deps and remediating anything with restrictive licenses or unknown provenance.
acceptance_criteria: OIDC client lib upgraded to a version with no critical/high CVEs and integration tests passing in staging
SAML toolkit upgraded and SAML end-to-end flows validated for major identity providers (Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin)
All services that vendor OpenSSL updated to patched binary/runtime with successful smoke tests and canary rollout plan
Configuration changes documented (cipher suites, TLS min versions) and rollout runbook added to Confluence
Supply-chain audit report submitted, flagged packages remediated or approved by security; any license conflicts documented with legal
No regressions in login latency (>10% increase) or token exchange error rate in canary window
work_items: Inventory services using OIDC/SAML clients and native OpenSSL bindings (control plane, console, auth proxy)
Create upgrade PRs for backend-auth (go) and auth-proxy (node) with bumped libs and migration notes
Run integration matrix against Okta/AzureAD/Google/Custom IdPs for SAML assert/ACS URLs
Prepare canary rollout targeting 10% of traffic with auto-rollback on error budget breach
Coordinate with infra for KMS/HSM compatibility testing and key rotation windows
Run license scanner (scancode/oss-review-toolkit) and produce remediation plan

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: API-breaking changes in newer SAML/OIDC clients could break third-party IdP integrations. Mitigation: maintain compatibility layer and run a matrix of integration tests against top 10 customer IdPs.
Risk: OpenSSL upgrade may change cipher defaults and trigger incompatibilities with older customer-managed clients. Mitigation: expose configurable TLS profiles and document deprecation timeline.
Risk: Supply-chain scanners produce false positives that slow rollout. Mitigation: legal/security triage workflow with SLAs for review decisions.
Risk: Increase in login latency due to additional crypto work. Mitigation: measure in canary and fallback to previous build with feature flag if >10% regression.
Risk: KMS/HSM integration differences. Mitigation: test rotations on a staging HSM and coordinate maintenance windows with customers if needed.
notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the SAML assertion parsing changes in PR #4529 — preserve legacy behaviour for 'aud' claim when possible.
Performance: benchmark key exchange and token validation on 4xA100 and 8xA10G to ensure no CPU regressions in the control plane.
Legal: review supply-chain report for any GPLv2-only components and propose acceptable remediation (replace/seek exception).
